source.title: Forgetting-MarI: LLM Unlearning via Marginal Information Regularization
source.authors: Shi-Zhou Xu; Yuan Ni; Stefan Broecker; Thomas Strohmer

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates a different unlearning method and compares forgetting and retained capability with a retain-only retraining baseline. It does not test the recovery attacks named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports target-set accuracy and general-capability results, plus a white-box training-membership detector result. The detector measures whether training exposure is detectable, not whether forgotten knowledge can be recovered. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-based recovery.
record.test_reason: This paper proposes a new unlearning method, Forgetting-MarI, and reports only its own performance against other unlearning methods. Its forgetting target is next-token accuracy on book text that matches a retain-only retrained model, not targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance. It runs no recovery attack: no relearning, activation ablation, quantization or prompting. It does not claim resistance to those attacks; its robustness claim concerns a white-box membership detector. It cites the Eight-Methods and Harry Potter papers only for protocol and context, so its results do not bear on any version of the shallow-unlearning claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Forgetting-MarI removes only the unlearn set's marginal information. They report that it matches the retain-only retrained model on forgetting, preserves general capability, and outperforms GA, GD, KL-GA and DPO, including under sequential (continual) unlearning. They also report that a white-box membership detector cannot separate it from the retrained model, consistent with their theoretical bounds.
record.recipe_differences: Forgetting-MarI uses a marginal-information regularizer with a retain-set KL utility term, rather than the cited gradient-ascent, preference-based, or other unlearning recipes. It is not a reproduction of the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report sensitivity to estimator choice and heterogeneous batches: position-wise MarI has higher variance and can over-unlearn at fixed trade-off settings, while pooled MarI is used by default. They also report dependence on regularization parameter and training epoch.

fits_no_version.finding: Forgetting-MarI matches the retain-only retrained model on retain, unlearn and validation next-token accuracy, with general benchmarks at or near that model's level.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Marginal-information unlearning approximates a retrain-on-retain model on copyrighted-text forgetting while preserving general capability, in GPT-2 Large and Llama-3.2-1B.

fits_no_version.finding: After Forgetting-MarI, the white-box min-k% detector's ROC-AUC closely matches that of the retain-only model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forgetting-MarI defeats perplexity-based membership detectors on the forgotten text.

record.problems: No recovery attack from versions B-E is tested. Target-set accuracy values are shown in figures and described relative to the retain-only baseline, but exact values are not stated in the text; the comparison does not establish near-chance accuracy. The detector result is figure-only and tests membership detection rather than knowledge recovery. Experiments use two mid-scale models and text datasets.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported general-capability table entries and submetrics are not separately extracted; the included benchmark rows provide examples of the reported retained-capability comparison. No results for versions B-E or F were reported as recovery-attack outcomes.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy is not measured (the target is retrain-baseline accuracy); no attack tests whether the knowledge can be recovered.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion.
No quantization of the unlearned weights.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery tests.
The method is not evaluated against any of the recovery attacks in B to E; robustness is claimed only against a perplexity-based membership detector.

missing.what: Continual unlearning results. The authors report KL-GA 'tends to relearn previously forgotten content' across sequential unlearning steps, while Forgetting-MarI keeps prior forgetting. This is relearning during later unlearning steps, not a deliberate relearning attack. Figure-only.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with an A-supports label is not justified. The A-linked rows are the authors' own method compared with other unlearning methods, and no row measures near-chance knowledge or recovery. The authors cite Eight-Methods (arXiv:2402.16835) and Who's Harry Potter only for protocol and context. The paper's 'provable undetectability' covers perplexity detectors only, not knowledge recovery.

versions.untested_parts: The study compares unlearn-set accuracy and general benchmarks, but does not test whether any attack recovers knowledge. Its reported comparison to the retain-only baseline does not establish that target accuracy is near chance.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or experiment showing that a method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No recovery tests using rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
The paper evaluates a white-box membership detector, but does not test resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.
